console: I build privacy and security projects around architecture, not slogans.
I keep looking below interfaces: identity, isolation, networks, trust boundaries, low-level behavior.
Browsers, cryptography, automation and infrastructure are where curiosity turns into real systems.
I care more about properties that can be verified than promises that live in a settings page.

thoth-browser.headline: Privacy as architecture, not a checklist of settings.
thoth-browser.overview: THOTH Browser treats privacy, anonymity and anti-correlation as architectural constraints. Identity is compartmentalized by context; storage, execution and network boundaries are explicit; routing can be separated; fingerprint resistance is treated as part of the model; and important properties are designed to be testable rather than merely asserted by the interface.

relayx.headline: Communication without identity becoming the product.
relayx.overview: RelayX is not just a private messenger. Identity, contacts, messages and files are designed to remain under local control, without a phone number, email address or public profile. Communication is built around Tor-only networking, end-to-end encryption and a blind relay that handles temporary opaque packets. The goal is to reduce metadata and correlation surfaces without sacrificing the fluidity expected from a modern messenger.
